issues.failure_explanation: In Case 3 (a rank-mixed point) the proof splits at the nearby point X_r into two sub-cases: either the first term of ||V|| is nonzero, or it vanishes. These give lower bounds (c_I/2)||∇f(X̲)×P_u||² and (1/2)Σ_k||∇f(X̲)_(k) P||² respectively. The proof then takes δ̄ as the minimum of the two bounds at X̲. Non-stationarity of X̲ only says that one of the two stationarity conditions fails. The first condition is ∇f(X̲)×_{k∉I}P_{u_k}=0 and the second is the normal-space condition for k∉I. So the first quantity can be 0 while the second is positive. Then δ̄=0 and δ(X̲)=0, contradicting δ>0. Sub-case A at X_r, where the first term is small but nonzero, gives no uniform positive bound, and the continuity argument only gives a bound by a quantity that is zero at X̲. The proof also assumes ||V_{X_r}||≠0 for nearby points without justifying it. A correct argument needs a lower bound that is positive whenever X̲ is non-stationary, e.g. one built on the maximum or on a combined quantity.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the min-based δ̄ with a lower bound that is positive at every non-stationary X̲. This needs a contained new argument that handles both sub-cases at X_r, for example by showing ||V_{X_r}||² ≥ a continuous combined quantity that vanishes only at stationary points, or by splitting on which condition fails at X̲.
issues.overall_effect: The sufficient decrease with δ>0 is not established for accumulation points in M_{≤r}∖(M_r∪M_{<r}) that are non-stationary only through the second condition. The convergence guarantee of GRAP-R at such mixed-rank points, which is the paper's claimed novelty, is not proved.
issues.title: Case 3 of the GRAP-R sufficient-decrease proof: the constant δ̄ can be zero at a non-stationary point
issues.why_classification: The method and conclusion should survive, but the repair needs a new nontrivial local lemma on the continuity of the tangent-cone projection norm near mixed-rank points. It is not a one-line fix.

issues.failure_explanation: By construction (eq: rfGRAP index), rfGRAP-R can lower each mode rank by at most one per iteration, so the candidate has rank r̆_k=r_k−1. If X̲ has underline r_k ≤ r_k−2 for some k∈I, then r̆_k>underline r_k. The proof nevertheless bounds ||V_{X_r̆}|| below by comparing the factors (ŭ_k, Ğ, Ğ†) of X_r̆ with (u̲_k, G̲, G̲†) of X̲ for all k∈[d], via continuity. When the ranks differ, the column spaces ŭ_k do not converge to u̲_k, the core G̃ has different dimensions, and Ğ† can blow up (the extra singular values are small). So the displayed lower bound by (1/2)||G̲×_k(P^⊥_{u̲_k}…G̲†)…|| and the resulting δ are unsupported in this regime. The cited 'similar to case 3 of GRAP-R' argument relied on X_r having exactly the rank of X̲, which GRAP-R achieves by projecting to X̲'s rank and rfGRAP-R cannot.

failure_location.quote: Consider $\breve{\vecr}=(\breve{r}_1,\breve{r}_2,\dots,\breve{r}_d)$ with $\breve{r}_k=\min\{r_k-1,\rank(\matx_{(k)})\}$ for $k\in I$ and $\breve{r}_k=r_k$ for $k\in[d]\setminus I$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either enlarge the rfGRAP-R candidate set to allow rank drops to Δ-rank, as in GRAP-R, and redo the proof, or supply a new argument showing sufficient decrease when only a one-step reduction is available and the reduced point is not rank-matched to X̲. The first option gives up the advertised 'only the smallest singular value' feature.
issues.overall_effect: The apocalypse-free guarantee for rfGRAP-R is unproved whenever an accumulation point has rank gap ≥2 in some mode relative to r. This is the generic over-estimated-rank situation motivating the paper.
issues.title: rfGRAP-R sufficient-decrease proof: the one-step rank-reduced candidate is not near X̲ in rank, so the continuity bounds are unsupported
issues.why_classification: Every supported fix either changes the algorithm and loses its key advertised cheaper rank-decreasing mechanism, or requires essentially new proof architecture for multi-step rank reduction. The convergence guarantee for the second main method is at stake.
